kernel.edit.patch.includes: StageManager.apply_patch of a one-node SetTransform: base_ir read, patch apply + validation, USD authoring into a new transaction layer.
kernel.edit.patch.excludes: Building the stage, JSON parsing, mesh extraction, Tier-1 QA, and the rollback that restores the base (untimed teardown).

kernel.edit.patch_qa.includes: apply_patch (one-node SetTransform) + StageManager.extract_meshes + tier1_qa, back to back.
kernel.edit.patch_qa.excludes: JSON parsing, harness state/QA persistence, rollback of the edit (untimed).

harness.edit.apply_scene_ir.includes: T.apply_scene_ir end to end for an accepted one-node SetTransform: JSON parse, transaction, extract_meshes + Tier-1 (in a worker thread), state/QA persistence to disk, session lock, event-loop hop.
harness.edit.apply_scene_ir.excludes: Session open, initial scene load, the undo that restores the base (untimed), MCP framing, any model call.

harness.edit.rejected_rollback.includes: T.apply_scene_ir given an edit that fails Tier-1 critically (adds an open, non-watertight quad via mesh_ref): transaction, extract_meshes + Tier-1, automatic rollback, state sync. Returns 'ROLLED BACK ...'.
harness.edit.rejected_rollback.excludes: Session open and scene load. Includes the cost of the Tier-1 pass that detects the failure, so it is the whole rejected-edit turn, not the rollback alone (see kernel.rollback.raw).

kernel.rollback.raw.includes: StageManager.rollback() of one pending one-node edit. Case discard=true is the path used for rejected edits (empties the layer in the same change block); discard=false is the path undo_last_edit uses. With include_next_read=true the timed region also contains the first extract_meshes() after the rollback.
kernel.rollback.raw.excludes: The edit that creates the pending transaction (untimed setup); Tier-1 QA.

harness.edit.undo.includes: T.undo_last_edit: lock, rollback of the top transaction, state invalidation, extract_meshes + Tier-1 re-run, QA persistence.
harness.edit.undo.excludes: The accepted edit that creates the transaction to undo (untimed setup).

harness.edit.to_pixels.includes: One agent turn of the edit loop: T.apply_scene_ir (accepted one-node edit) followed by T.render_preview (4-view clay contact sheet, 256 px per view, wireframe on = the tool defaults, PNG save, fake upload, preview bookkeeping).
harness.edit.to_pixels.excludes: The undo that restores the base (untimed), visual QA, any model call.

harness.qa.visual_overhead.includes: T.run_visual_qa against FakeDecisionsClient with a current preview: approval revocation + QA persistence, request construction, the fake client call (validation + canned answers), score composition, audit-delta, state write. Tool-side overhead only.
harness.qa.visual_overhead.excludes: Model/API latency (none is incurred), rendering the preview (rendered once, untimed, before the loop). The fake client's own share is reported in extra.fake_client_ms_median.

kernel.raster.contact_sheet.includes: kernel.raster.contact_sheet: 4 views (front, right, top, persp), wireframe overlay on, label + border drawing, sheet assembly (PIL image returned).
kernel.raster.contact_sheet.excludes: Mesh extraction from USD, PNG encoding/saving, upload. Scenes are 12 spheres on a 4x3 grid (triangle count is the closest to the target the sphere segment count allows).

kernel.som.marked_sheet.includes: kernel.som.marked_contact_sheet: 4 views rendered with render_buffers, set-of-mark badge placement per view, labels, sheet assembly.
kernel.som.marked_sheet.excludes: Mesh extraction, PNG encoding, any model call that would consume the marked sheet.

kernel.uv.unwrap.includes: fast_ops.unwrap_uvs (xatlas unwrap + pack + stretch statistics) at 1024 px/m and the default 2048 atlas resolution.
kernel.uv.unwrap.excludes: Writing UVs to USD, LOD generation. Convex spheres and one concave U prism.

kernel.lod.generate.includes: fast_ops.generate_lods with default ratios (1.0, 0.5, 0.25, 0.1): meshoptimizer simplify + cache/overdraw/fetch optimisation per level. with_uvs=true is the pipeline's call (seam-split points + UVs from unwrap, attribute-aware simplify); with_uvs=false is the weld-first path.
kernel.lod.generate.excludes: UV unwrap (done once, untimed, for the with_uvs cases), writing LODs anywhere.

kernel.collider.convex.includes: fast_ops.generate_colliders (max_hulls=8) on convex closed meshes: topology check, scipy ConvexHull, the 'fast_path' (CoACD is not invoked).
kernel.collider.convex.excludes: Hull authoring into USD/GLB. Only the convex spheres are run here; the concave mesh is kernel.collider.concave.

kernel.collider.concave.includes: fast_ops.generate_colliders (max_hulls=8) on a concave U-shaped prism: topology check, CoACD decomposition (threshold 0.05, the package's settings), per-part hull.
kernel.collider.concave.excludes: Hull authoring. CoACD may use threads that OMP_NUM_THREADS does not cap; extra.process_cpu_over_wall shows whether it did.

kernel.export.pipeline.includes: fast_ops.run_export_pipeline: unwrap_scene (xatlas, one atlas per material) + generate_lods per mesh + generate_colliders. This is the 'UV + LOD + collider outside Blender' figure.
kernel.export.pipeline.excludes: Package writing/validation, USD authoring, mesh extraction (meshes are prepared untimed). Per-stage medians from ExportBundle.timings_ms are in extra.parts_median_ms.

kernel.qa.tier1.includes: fast_ops.tier1_qa on the crate and barrel meshes (topology, budgets, grounding, pairwise AABB/contact checks).
kernel.qa.tier1.excludes: Mesh extraction from USD (meshes prepared untimed).

kernel.validate.usd.includes: Three separate checks on the written package USD of the crate/barrel: validate_usd(stage) (all registered UsdValidation validators), check_engine_compliance(stage, meshes, budget) (unreal_5 rules, texture size/convention, hulls), and validate_usd(path) which also opens the file.
kernel.validate.usd.excludes: Writing the package. The stage is the package's own USD (LOD variants, colliders, textured materials).

kernel.package.write.includes: kernel.package.write_engine_package on a fresh stage: UV authoring, textures copied/converted (unreal_5 DirectX normal flip), USD + USDZ + GLB LODs + collider GLB, inspector HTML, hashing, and the function's built-in validation (UsdValidation, engine compliance, cold package validation).
kernel.package.write.excludes: Stage creation (untimed setup), the UV/LOD/collider bundle (computed once, untimed), deleting the package (untimed teardown). Texture inputs: textured=true gives every material 3 maps (albedo, ORM, normal) from FakeImageBackend + derive_pbr at 256 px (the size the offline pipeline produces); textured=false has no texture inputs, which skips texture copy/flip and the PNG encoding of textures into every GLB.

kernel.package.write_large_textures.includes: ONE SAMPLE, NO WARM-UP (too slow to repeat): the same write_engine_package call as kernel.package.write for the crate with 1024 px albedo/ORM/normal maps per material (384 px in --quick), to show how packaging time scales with texture size.
kernel.package.write_large_textures.excludes: Stage creation, bundle computation, texture generation (all untimed). A single sample is not a distribution: n=1, p95 null, and the first call also pays any first-use costs.

kernel.package.validate_cold.includes: validators.validate_package on an already written package directory: manifest + hash check of every file, USD re-open, UV/texture/LOD/collider consistency checks, GLB material checks.
kernel.package.validate_cold.excludes: Writing the package (once, untimed). Same textured packages as kernel.package.write.

kernel.settle.includes: kernel.settle.settle: 10 movable props (boxes, cylinders, spheres; 3 stacked above others) dropped onto a static floor slab, iterating to convergence.
kernel.settle.excludes: Applying the resulting offsets as IR ops, mesh extraction. Meshes are built directly from compile_ir primitives.

kernel.spatial.build.includes: Octree construction. constructor=SpatialIndex(meshes) takes world-space MeshData (per-mesh bounds + tree); constructor=from_bounds takes precomputed PrimInfo (what StageManager uses). constructor=stage_first_query is StageManager.query_region right after an edit, i.e. USD traversal + from_bounds + one query.
kernel.spatial.build.excludes: Building the input mesh list / PrimInfo list (untimed). Boxes are 1 m cubes on a 1.5 m grid.

kernel.spatial.query_region.includes: SpatialIndex.query_region(...) + RegionResult.to_text(1200) on a prebuilt index, for a small, a medium and a whole-scene region; plus StageManager.query_region on a 200-node stage with the index already cached.

kernel.cache.hit.includes: tactics.cached.cached_export_pipeline on a populated LocalBlobStore: ir_subtree_key/node_key hashing, blob read, npz decode into an ExportBundle, hit accounting.
kernel.cache.hit.excludes: The original compute. Local disk store only (no GCS tier). extra.miss_over_hit_median_ratio compares with kernel.cache.miss.

kernel.cache.miss.includes: cached_export_pipeline on an empty store (fresh directory per iteration): key hashing, run_export_pipeline, bundle npz encode, blob write, then decode of the returned bundle.

ipc.blender_pool.fake.includes: STAND-IN ONLY, IPC OVERHEAD ONLY: BlenderPool(1, fake=True) (a CPython daemon, no bpy, no Blender). Case op=ping is one request/response over the socketpair; op=render_1024x1024x4_f32 requests a fake render and reads the 16.8 MB float32 image back through shared memory (the daemon synthesises the gradient with numpy: that cost is included).
ipc.blender_pool.fake.excludes: Everything about real Blender: start-up, scene import, rendering. These numbers say nothing about real render time. Pool start-up is excluded.

mcp.roundtrip.apply_scene_ir.includes: tools/call apply_scene_ir (accepted one-node SetTransform) through the real MCP stdio server (python -m antigravity3d.runtime.mcp_server, offline) driven by the official mcp client: client framing, pipe I/O, server dispatch + session gate + the tool itself. extra.direct_median_ms is the same tool called in-process on an identical session (base scene applied as one open transaction, as over MCP); extra.mcp_overhead_ms = mcp median - direct median.
mcp.roundtrip.apply_scene_ir.excludes: Server start-up/handshake/open_asset_session (reported in extra, not in samples), the undo between iterations (untimed). The server is a separate process, so its CPU competes with the client on this 4-vCPU box.

pipeline.prop_to_engine.offline.includes: PropToEngineDAG.run wall time (in-process, same wiring as `agy3d prop --offline`, bare event-loop start included, unreal_5, max_rounds=4) per prompt x mode x cache state. cache=cold: fresh output dir; cache=warm: second run on the same dir/cache (route decision and image/PBR/export results reused); Per-node durations and fixture shares are in extra, with process CPU time (all threads) per run. For the fixture-free figure see pipeline.prop.replayed_images.
pipeline.prop_to_engine.offline.excludes: Interpreter start (see cli.*), Blender, any real network wait. Fixture time (fake image synthesis in a worker thread, fake judge validation) IS inside the wall time. extra.wall_outside_fixture_spans_ms is wall minus the union of fixture spans; local work that runs concurrently inside a fixture span (geometry beside speculative PBR) is subtracted too, so it is only a lower bound on local work, not 'local compute'.

pipeline.prop.replayed_images.includes: HEADLINE fixture-free pipeline figure: PropToEngineDAG.run wall time with a fresh output dir and cache (cold) where FakeImageBackend returns, instantly, the bytes the cold run already generated, so no procedural image synthesis runs. Same prompts, modes and repeats as pipeline.prop_to_engine.offline. extra has process CPU time (all threads) for this run and for the cold run.
pipeline.prop.replayed_images.excludes: Image synthesis (removed). Still included: the fake decisions client (request wire validation, canned answers) and the plane's own request/answer handling, route, USD staging and edits, Tier-1 QA, raster/contact sheets and set-of-mark sheets, UV/LOD/collider, packaging and validation, inspector, report writing, event-loop and thread hops, cache hashing and blob I/O. Interpreter start.

pipeline.prop_to_engine.node_classificat.includes: Derived from the same runs as pipeline.prop_to_engine.offline (cold cache only): for each DAG node, the median share of its own duration during which a fixture call (fake image synthesis or fake judge) was in progress. A node is 'fixture-dominated' when that share is >= 0.5, otherwise 'local deterministic work'. The 'samples' are the per-run cold wall times.
pipeline.prop_to_engine.node_classificat.excludes: Warm runs. A node's wall duration overlaps other nodes (pbr runs beside geometry), so node durations do not sum to wall time. Shares assume node windows from DagReport and fixture spans use the same clock (they do, to within the event-loop start-up of Dag.run).

cli.prop.offline.includes: Subprocess wall time of `agy3d prop "wooden crate with iron brackets" --offline --out DIR` (fresh DIR each run): console-script start, imports, the whole offline pipeline, report printing, process exit.
cli.prop.offline.excludes: Nothing in-process is subtracted: this is what a shell user waits for. Exit status 0 is required (preview gates passed).

cli.models.includes: Subprocess wall time of `agy3d models` (prints a static table): console-script start + CLI module imports + exit. A proxy for CLI cold start.
cli.models.excludes: Pipeline work. Not a warm number: each run is a new interpreter (OS file cache is warm after the first run, which is kept).

import.usd_stage.includes: In a fresh interpreter: perf_counter around `import antigravity3d.kernel.usd_stage` only (pxr + numpy + package imports it pulls in), measured inside the child. extra.bare_interpreter_wall_ms is `python -c pass` subprocess wall time for reference.
import.usd_stage.excludes: Interpreter start-up (reported separately). First-call lazy costs (UsdValidation registry load, etc.) are not included.

throughput.prop_offline.includes: K distinct offline prop runs (PropToEngineDAG, governed mode, unreal_5; prompt/author seed vary per job, each job has its own empty cache dir) executed by P spawned worker processes (ProcessPoolExecutor, spawn). One timed sample per P: wall time from submitting the K jobs to the last result.
throughput.prop_offline.excludes: Worker start-up and module imports (workers are started and warmed first). This is the deterministic local portion with fixture images and fixture judges, not a live throughput figure: a live run waits on APIs and would overlap differently. 4 vCPUs only, so P=4 contends with the parent and anything else on the box.

extra.design_doc_claim: 120+ assets/hour on 8 workers (not comparable: 4 vCPUs, fixtures)
120+ assets/hour on 8 workers (not comparable: 4 vCPUs, fixtures)
120+ assets/hour on 8 workers (not comparable: 4 vCPUs, fixtures)

dag.batch_sanitize.includes: BatchSanitizeDAG.run over generated meshes (load, Tier-1 before, shape-preserving repair, Tier-1 after, UV+LOD+collider export pipeline, USD+GLB write, UsdValidation + engine compliance) with max_parallel=jobs, unreal_5 default budget. One timed sample per jobs value: wall time of the whole batch.
dag.batch_sanitize.excludes: Mesh generation (untimed). The DAG runs each file in a worker process (jobs = number of workers; one worker even at jobs=1, for crash isolation), so the wall time includes about a second of worker start-up per jobs value. Meshes above 15,000 triangles exceed the default unreal_5 tri budget and are reported 'needs_attention'; that is a property of the inputs, listed in extra.status_counts / extra.attention_reasons.

extra.per_mesh_sum_of_stage_ms_note: each mesh's own load+repair+export+validate stage times; overlap when jobs>1
